PluginData.Author: TomasServo
PluginData.Tooltip: Streams atomic.fm from Icecast into the Space Engineers client.
PluginData.Description:
atomic.fm streams a configurable Icecast URL through the local Windows audio device.
Any terminal block can be an atomic.fm sound source. You do not need to place a vanilla Sound Block. Planters, lights, antennas, LCDs, doors, cockpits, cargo containers, refineries, assemblers, and most functional blocks can act as radio anchors if they have Custom Data.
To make a block emit atomic.fm: 1. Enable atomic.fm in Pulsar. 2. Aim at the block and open the terminal/control panel. 3. Select the exact block in the terminal list. 4. Find the block's Custom Data field. 5. Add the required marker on its own line: atomic.fm=true 6. Optional: set how far away the block can be heard: atomic.fm.range=35 7. Optional: set this block's loudness before distance fade: atomic.fm.volume=1.0 8. Close the terminal and stand near the block. 9. The stream starts automatically when atomic.fm finds a marked block. 10. Move away to hear distance fade. Turn around the block to hear left/right stereo panning.
Custom Data options: - atomic.fm=true enables the block as a radio anchor. - atomic.fm.range sets the audible range in meters. Default fallback is 50. - atomic.fm.volume sets that block's local loudness from 0.0 to 1.0. Default is 1.0.
Controls: - Ctrl+Alt+J toggles playback manually. - Start atomic.fm and Stop atomic.fm are also available in plugin settings. - If you manually stop playback, atomic.fm will stay stopped for that game session.
Notes: - Audio is client-side. Each player chooses whether to install and enable the plugin. - Marked blocks act as ambient radio anchors with distance fade and stereo panning. - The audio is not sent through the game server and does not replace vanilla Sound Block audio. - Plain armor blocks cannot be used because they do not have terminal Custom Data. - If no marked blocks exist, manual playback still works through the local Windows audio device.
